task.title: Font variants and features
task.shortdesc: Many fonts have alternate letter shapes, number styles, ligatures and other features. Use the properties of this topic to ask for them. The font must provide a feature for CSSMedia to use it.

context.p: An OpenType font stores its features in tables, and each feature has a four-letter tag, such as liga for the common ligatures. The properties font-variant-* and font-kerning ask for groups of features by name. The property font-feature-settings sets one feature by its tag.
The element names in the examples, such as term and formula, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

info.p: Use font-kerning to turn kerning on or off. The values auto and normal use the kerning of the font, and none turns it off:

Use font-variant-ligatures to control the ligatures. The value normal uses the defaults of the font: common ligatures and contextual forms are on, and discretionary and historical ligatures are off. The value none turns off all of them. You can also combine one value from each pair:

ul.li: common-ligatures or no-common-ligatures, for ligatures such as "fi" and "fl".
discretionary-ligatures or no-discretionary-ligatures, for optional ligatures that suit a particular style.
historical-ligatures or no-historical-ligatures.
contextual or no-contextual, for glyphs that change with the characters around them.

stepxmp.pre: body { font-variant-ligatures: common-ligatures discretionary-ligatures; } code { font-variant-ligatures: none; }

info.p: The ligatures that a script needs, such as those of Arabic, are always used.
Use font-variant-caps to ask for small capitals and other forms of capital letters:

ul.li: small-caps: small capitals instead of lowercase letters.
all-small-caps: small capitals instead of lowercase and uppercase letters.
petite-caps and all-petite-caps: the same with petite capitals, which are smaller.
unicase: small capitals for the uppercase letters, and normal lowercase letters.
titling-caps: capitals designed for titles.
normal: the usual letters.

info.p: When the font has no small capitals, CSSMedia creates them by scaling the capitals, unless font-synthesis-small-caps is none.

Use font-variant-position to ask for subscript glyphs with sub or superscript glyphs with super. The value normal uses the ordinary glyphs. When the font has no such glyphs, CSSMedia scales and moves the ordinary glyphs, unless font-synthesis-position is none. The @font-face descriptors that Font resources and descriptors explains can change their size and position.
Use font-variant-numeric to choose the shape and the spacing of numbers. Combine one value from each group:

ul.li: lining-nums or oldstyle-nums: figures as high as capitals, or figures with ascenders and descenders.
proportional-nums or tabular-nums: figures with different widths, or with equal widths. Use equal widths in tables so that the digits line up.
diagonal-fractions or stacked-fractions: fractions with a diagonal slash, or with the numerator above the denominator.
ordinal: the forms of the suffixes of ordinal numbers, such as "st" in "1st".
slashed-zero: a zero with a slash.

info.p: Fonts can have several alternate shapes for a character, which the font identifies by numbers. Use font-variant-alternates to ask for them. The value normal asks for none. Otherwise combine these values:

ul.li: historical-forms: historical glyph forms.
stylistic(name): a stylistic alternate.
styleset(name, ...): one or more stylistic sets.
character-variant(name, ...): variants of individual characters.
swash(name): a swash form.
ornaments(name): an ornament.
annotation(name): an annotation form, such as a circled digit.

info.p: The names are yours. You define each name for a font family with @font-feature-values. The prelude of the rule lists one or more family names, which cannot be generic families. Inside the block, a rule for each kind of alternate maps names to numbers:
A name that is not defined for the family of the text has no effect. Names are case-sensitive. If you define the same name twice, the last definition wins. These are the rules of the block:

ul.li: @stylistic maps a name to one number for the feature salt.
@historical-forms maps a name to one or more numbers for hist.
@styleset maps a name to one or more numbers from 1 to 99, for the features ss01 to ss99. A 0 or a number above 99 selects no feature.
@character-variant maps a name to one or two numbers. The first, from 1 to 99, selects cv01 to cv99, and the optional second sets its value. A 0 or a number above 99 selects no feature.
@swash maps a name to one number for swsh or cswh.
@ornaments maps a name to one number for ornm.
@annotation maps a name to one number for nalt.

step.cmd: Choose forms for a language or a script

info.p: Use font-variant-east-asian to choose the forms of Chinese and Japanese characters. The value normal asks for none. Otherwise combine a glyph form, a width and ruby:

ul.li: jis78, jis83, jis90 and jis04: the Japanese forms of that edition of the JIS standard.
simplified and traditional: the forms of simplified and traditional Chinese.
full-width and proportional-width: glyphs of equal width, or with proportional spacing.
ruby: glyphs designed for the small size of ruby text.

info.p: Use font-variant-emoji to choose between the text and the emoji forms of the characters that have both. The value text asks for the text form, emoji for the emoji form and unicode for the default form that Unicode gives to each character. The value normal lets CSSMedia choose. A variation selector in the text, U+FE0E for text and U+FE0F for emoji, overrides the property.

A font can have different glyphs for different languages. CSSMedia chooses the language system of the font from the language of the text, which comes from xml:lang or from -cssmedia-lang. Use font-language-override only when the font lacks the language system for your text but has another that suits it. The value is the OpenType language system tag in a string, such as "SRB" for Serbian. It is not a language tag such as sr. The tag has four characters, and CSSMedia pads shorter tags with spaces. A tag that the font does not have is ignored. The value normal uses the language of the text.

step.cmd: Use the shorthand and the feature tags

info.p: Use font-variant to set several variant properties in one declaration. It takes normal, none, or values of the longhand properties. The value none sets font-variant-ligatures to none. The properties that you do not write return to their initial values. The shorthand does not change font-language-override, font-feature-settings or font-variation-settings:

stepxmp.pre: body { font-variant: small-caps; } table { font-variant: lining-nums tabular-nums; }

info.p: Use font-feature-settings when no other property describes the feature that you need. The value is normal, or a comma-separated list of tags. A tag is a string of four characters, followed by an optional number, on or off. Without a value, a tag is on. The value 0 or off turns the feature off, and a positive number turns it on and selects its alternate:

Tags are case-sensitive. A tag that the font does not have is ignored. If a tag occurs more than once, the last value wins. The settings of this property come after the settings of the other properties, so they win. Prefer a higher-level property, such as font-variant-ligatures, when it describes the feature.
